sources.citation: Usher, Timothy (Santa Fe Institute). n.d. [page last modified 2024-06-25]. Kenati. In: Newguineaworld (comparative Papuan languages site, hosted by Universität Zürich), families: Trans-New Guinea > Eastern Highlands-Kratke Range > Eastern Highlands > Kainantu > Kenati.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.source_kind: database or survey citing another work
sources.note: Explicit negative: the Phonology section consists of the single sentence 'There is no published phonology of Kenati.' Sources named are Gajdusek 1980: 145-146 (59 body-part terms, Arabunkara) and Dodd (n.d.) survey vocabulary of 'Azana' supplied as a comparative spreadsheet by Paul Whitehouse via SIL Ukarumpa; six pronouns given in phonetic form (1sg naʔe, 2sg aʔe, 3sg urɛrike/ijake, 1pl tire, 2pl anta, 3pl urɛri ɪntea arʌðe) without stress or tone marks; 'Nothing is known about Kenati verbal morphology besides what little can be gleaned from the third person forms in Dodd's vocabulary.' Clas…

sources.citation: Mission Network News (davidvranish). 2004-12-16. 'Tribe in Papua New Guinea to receive completed New Testament translation.' [interview with Mike Henderson, New Tribes Mission, on the Aziana New Testament].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing linguistic. Value: first-hand confirmation from the translator that NTM devised a written form and vernacular literacy programme for Aziana ('We taught them how to read and write their own language, and trained teachers'), i.e. an orthography statement and primers exist in NTM/Ethnos360 hands -- strengthens A's pointer (work 2).

sources.citation: New Tribes Mission [Henderson, Mike & Diane, translators]. 2004. Kaji werumuri emi nänangi'e [Aziana (Kenati) New Testament]. Papua New Guinea: New Tribes Mission. (c) 2004 Global Partners Alliance per find.bible (id GATNTM); text and Faith Comes By Hearing audio online at Bible.is as '2004 New Tribes Mission'.
sources.access_detail: read online, no copy kept
sources.note: No description: connected primary text (whole NT, plus dramatized audio) in a practical Latin orthography with ä and apostrophe (e.g. 'Matyu Jisas wä'näbänäni Pwei'na Pawe'na Emunäni ya wo Matyu woki täräve'iyero'mu'e'); no stress or tone marks evident in the sample and nothing states what the apostrophe or ä encode. Raw data for a future phonetic study, not a statement.

sources.citation: Gajdusek, D. Carleton. 1980. Journal of further explorations in the Kuru Region and in the Kukukuku Country, Eastern Highlands of Eastern New Guinea and of a return to West New Guinea: December 25, 1963 to May 4, 1964. Bethesda, MD: NIH (Study of Child Growth and Development and Disease Patterns in Primitive Cultures). Genatei entries 26-29 March 1964, pp. 142-151.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Ethnographic travel journal (Glottolog 'minimal'): three Genatei villages (Yabuiara, Oropina, Arabunkara), impressionistic remarks that the language 'is clearly closely related to Fore', a 'Fore-Tairora mixture' with 'frequent terminal o', three vocabulary items (sapa 'sweet potato', namo 'house', yabi 'sugar'); mentions Nagra tape recordings of Arubunkara singsings. No linguistic description.

Kainantu-Goroka, Kainantu. Lg Dev: NT: 2005.'; web edition 2016 'Language Development NT: 2005. Writing Latin script'.

sources.citation: Wurm, Stephen A. 1975. Eastern Central Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene, 461-526. Pacific Linguistics C-38. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Kenati stress. pp. 466, 472-473: Kenati (Ganati, Aziana) formerly a phylum-level isolate, tentatively a family-level isolate in the East New Guinea Highlands Stock on Lloyd's (1973) lexicostatistics; 'in the absence of structural information on Kenati, this has to remain preliminary'. Sec. 2.7.2.2.5.8 'The Kenati Family', p. 491: 'Very little is known of the structure of Kenati'. The 'Suprasegmentals' paragraphs in this chapter belong to the Wiru (p. 489) and Angan sketches, not Kenati (the earlier nort2920 record's attribution of one to Kenati was wrong).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid kena1250 (Hammarström, Forkel, Haspelmath & Bank), and Glottolog reference 311592 (Lloyd 1973) record.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic only. Glottolog 5.3 lists exactly two references (Gajdusek 1980; Lloyd 1973: 93), the same two as Glottolog 5.1; no phonology, wordlist, sketch or grammar doctype for gat in any provider including silpng. Endangerment note: 'Aziana (gat-gat) = 5* (Developing)' from Ethnologue 2025.

sources.citation: Lloyd, Richard G. 1973. The Angan language family, sec. 2.16 'Neighbouring languages', pp. 93-94 (+ name list p. 106, word-list credits p. 107). In Karl J. Franklin (ed.), The linguistic situation in the Gulf District and adjacent areas, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-26. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Glottolog Glottolog's most extensive description. Two paragraphs on Kenati: population 536 'downstream from Wonenara', origin stories (descendants of Baruya and Fore/Gimi), cognate percentages on 170 words (Gimi 19%, Fore 17%, Owena 19%, Awa 12%, Tairora 14%, Waffa 12%; 4-6% with Angan languages), and two roots (taa 'brother', naano 'sister'). Name list p. 106: 'KENATI (Azianan) Ganati (Wurm 1964); Asena or Aziana (Government)'. p. 107 credits the Kenati survey word list to L. Dodd (SIL), unpublished; the list itself is not printed. No phonology, no stress.
